The peak is on the completing token and single-token replacements that break the fixed expression sharply reduce activation.

Develop a comprehensive guide in a step-by-step format for individuals interested in making their own bath salts. Provide details on the necessary ingredients and tools needed, recommended measurement ratios and descriptions of the benefits of the different types of salts, essential oils and herbs commonly used. Ensure that the guide is informative and easy to follow, and include any relevant safety precautions that should be considered during the process. Additionally, provide tips for storing and using the finished product.<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
Step-by-Step Guide for Making Bath Salts:

1. Gather your ingredients and tools. You will need:

- Epsom salt or sea salt (or a mixture of both)
- Baking soda
- Essential oils (choose your favorites or based on their therapeutic properties)
- Dried herbs or flower petals (optional)
- A mixing bowl
- A measuring cup and spoons
- A jar or container for storage

2. Decide on the ratio of salts and baking soda. A common ratio is 2:1 (two parts salts to one part baking soda). For example, if you want to make one cup of bath salts, you will need 2/3 cup of salts and 1/3 cup of baking soda.

3. Add the salts and baking soda to the mixing bowl and stir together. Make sure there are no clumps.

4. Add in your chosen essential oils. Start with a few drops (3-5 drops) and gradually add more until you reach your desired scent strength. Mix well.

5. If using dried herbs, add to the mixture and stir well. You can use lavender, chamomile, rose petals, or any other herbs that you find soothing or relaxing.

6. Transfer the mixture to a container or jar for storage. Make sure the lid is properly closed to prevent moisture from getting in.

7. Label your bath salts jar or container with the date and ingredients.

Safety precautions: 

- Make sure your essential oils and herbs are safe for use in bath products, as some may cause skin irritation or allergic reactions.
- Do a patch test on a small area of skin before using the bath salts all over your body.
- Keep the bath salts out of reach of children and pets.
- Do not ingest the bath salts.

Tips for storage and usage:

- Store your bath salts in a cool, dry place to prevent clumping.
- You can use about 1/4 to 1/2 cup of bath salts per bath. Add the salts to the water as it fills up the tub, so they dissolve properly.
- Soak in the bath for 20-30 minutes for the best benefits.
- Rinse off with warm water after soaking to remove any leftover salt residue.
- Use your bath salts within six months to ensure freshness.<|im_end|>

At TSM plumbing and drainage, our skilled engineers are often asked this question, to be able to explain it. We have to start with, what is the construction of your current drainage system from your home. The majority of older domestic drainage systems within the UK are either made up of 100 mm or 150 mm vitrified clay pipe, modern housing stock use plastic pipe joined with rubber sealed couplings, and in the main these systems do the job, with regard to carrying waste, and in many cases, storm water from one point to another. However, we need to look at whether they are carrying out their function to the optimum capacity. The unfortunate truth is most drainage systems even modern ones will have some sort of defect such as a misalignment of joints, dipped sections of pipework, stepped joints, they may even have fine root ingress, the pipes may also be fracturing or leaking. But even with all these faults, more often than not, they keep on working.
It is often the case that drains become blocked and then clear themselves due to the weight of water that builds up in the pipeline behind the blockage, in some cases, the drains operate like a septic tank and dependent on the ground conditions, the majority of the waste water soaks away into the subsoil through either a defective joint or a fracture in the pipe, while the remaining solids and waste breakdown within the remaining pipework.
The following is a typical example that we at TSM, plumbing and drainage find, a family buy an older property from an elderly couple, who are downsizing to accommodation more suited to their needs. The drains have been working fine for the previous owners. However, once a family with children, and all the associated baths, showers, washing machines and dishwashers that are now used within the property on a very regular basis. The drainage system can no longer cope, and the defects come to light, it is always a good idea to get a drainage survey when purchasing an older property. Unfortunately, at present, most people settle for a standard house survey, which does not include the drains. We will be looking at a later date at what is undertaken on a house drainage survey and the likely costs that you may incur.
Common causes of blocked drains.
One of the most common causes of a blocked drain is Grease and Fat, which builds up within the domestic drain over many years, it is like cholesterol in the arteries over time the pipes narrow due to build up and cause a blockage. Before you throw your old chip fat or grease from the frying pan down the sink, consider other ways of disposing of it in a more environmentally friendly manner and in turn, it may save you money, so that you do not need to call out a drainage engineer to clear the grease and fat that you poured down your sink.

Italian seasonings of oregano and basil combine with red and green lentils to give this hearty soup its great flavor and high fiber content. Add Italian sausage and red wine for a full-bodied meal.
Green and Red Lentils, Rice, Onion, Carrot, Celery, Leek, Paprika and Spices. No added salt, preservatives or MSG.
Rinse, drain and pick over lentils.
Heat olive oil in a 6 or 8-quart pot.
Crumble and brown sausage in oil, breaking up clumps with flat end of metal spatula.
Stir in contents of Indiana Harvest Sausage and Lentil Soup Mix seasoning packet.
Add lentils and broth. Bring pot to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover and simmer 30 minutes.
Add tomatoes, zucchini, and wine. Bring back to a simmer, cover and cook 30 minutes.
For a twist, a box of frozen, chopped spinach may be substituted for the zucchini! This is a beautiful country supper!
To boost vegetables, add 2 cups chopped kale, spinach, or mushrooms in final 30 minutes of cooking time.
To boost fruit, add 3/4 cup raisins or 1 diced apple with tomatoes.
To cut saturated fat and sodium, halve the amount of sausage and prepare with low-fat, lower sodium chicken sausage as substitute for Italian pork sausage, or substitute 1 pound extra lean ground turkey or beef plus ½ teaspoon each salt-free garlic powder, onion powder and black pepper, or go Vegetarian.
To cut sodium, prepare with no salt added canned diced tomatoes and low sodium broth. To cut sodium further, substitute water for half of the broth.
You will use red and green bell pepper, onion, eggplant, and vegetable broth for a delicious soup with a ratatouille twist.
Optional: Add more veggies to taste! Feel free to experiment with your favorites.
Sauté vegetables on medium heat in 6 or 8-quart pot.
Add lentils, vegetable packet, and broth to pot.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer covered for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes.
In large skillet crumble and brown sausage in oil, stir in contents of seasoning packet.
Rinse, drain and pick over lentils, place into slow cooker and stir well.
Cover and cook on High 4-5 hours.
Add tomatoes, zucchini and wine and continue on HI 1 hour.
*This soup takes less than 2 hours to make on the stove, so the slow cooker may not offer much convenience.
On Saute setting heat oil and cook sausage lightly. Use a metal spatula to break up clumps.
Stir in lentils, contents of the seasoning packet, 2-3 diced zucchini, 1 28-oz can tomato pieces.
Add 4 cups beef broth, but do not exceed the 2/3 capacity on the cook pot.
Set the pressure cooker for 20 minutes.
Use quick or natural release, open pot and stir in 4 additional cups beef broth, 1 cup red wine and 2 cups water. Stir well.
Cook on saute setting with open pot 5-10 minutes and serve.

Отдых на море. Что может быть прекраснее? А какое море выбрать для отдыха с ребенком? Черное, Азовское, Средиземное? Друг блога «Развивашка» — Настя Кондратовец расскажет нам о своем отдыхе с ребенком на Азовском море в Кирилловке в 2012 году.
Первоначально мы планировали поехать в сентябре в Крым. Но все знакомые убеждали: «Черное море холодное для ребенка», поэтому мы взяли путевку на базу «Чайка» в Кирилловке.
База находится на начале косы Пересыпь, на самом берегу моря, в десяти минутах ходьбы от нее расположен главный рынок, ночной клуб, луна-парк.
Цена отдыха на Азовском море в 2012 году
Примерная стоимость проживания одного человека в номере за 10 дней, включая питание зависит от типа номера:
- Стандарт 80 $
- Полулюкс 120 $.
- Люкс 160 $
В стандартной комнате на 2-х человек находится 3 кровати, тумбочки, стол, шкаф телевизор, кондиционер. Душ (работает по часам), туалет находятся в соседней пристройке. Полулюкс и люкс и отличаются наличием санузла, водопровода, и еще одной комнаты. Корпуса старые, но номера ухоженные, выполнен ремонт. В номерах нужно самому поддерживать порядок.
Отдых на Азовском море — база «Чайка» в Кирилловке
База «Чайка» занимает небольшую территорию. Помимо жилых зданий на ней находится кафе/бар, здание столовой и площадка. Днем на площадке развлекаются дети, а по вечерам там бывает дискотека.
Для детей есть еще детская площадка с качелями и небольшими городками из лестниц и горок.
Над пляжем идет галерея, во время шторма по ней можно гулять, любуясь морем и не рискуя намокнуть.
Питание в столовой для всех отдыхающих одинаковое, сбалансированное. В меню ежедневно присутствуют супы, овощи, фрукты, мясо, молочные продукты, на ужин давали сладкие булочки. Кормили сытно и вкусно.
Азовское и Черное моря
Главная достопримечательность Кирилловки – море. Оно истинно детское, теплое и мелкое. Визуально вода чистая, мусор не плавает, цвет естественный морской. Довольно долго глубина не превышает метра и дети могут спокойно плескаться в воде, пока родители загорают на песочке. Морское дно песчаное, поэтому когда заходишь по пояс, то дна и стоп уже не видно.
Черное море, конечно, прозрачнее Азовского моря. Но, ученые утверждают, что чистота воды определяется не только прозрачностью, но и биохимическим составом. В водах Азовского моря содержится 92 химических элемента, которые легко проникают в кожу и способствуют оздоровлению организма человека.
По ночам, вода в Азоском море фосфорится — это очень красивое зрелище.
Кроме того, целебным является и песок на побережье Азовского моря, врачи рекомендуют принимать солнечные ванны прямо на песке, без всяких ковриков и подстилок.
У нас был замечательный пляж из ракушек, перетертых в песок. Встречались и насыпи из целых раковин — детки с удовольствием игрались там.
На пляже есть урны и лавочки, в поисках тени можно расположиться под галереей. А раздевалок, к сожалению нет.

There was more struggling, and then a passing railroad hand came to the detective's assistance. Together they hurried him toward the depot, and there discovering the local officer, turned him over. It was with a torn coat, scarred hands and face, and a black eye that Sebastian was locked up for the night.

When the children came home they could not say what had happened to their brother, but as nine o'clock struck, and then ten and eleven, and Sebastian did not return, Mrs. Gerhardt was beside herself. He had stayed out many a night as late as twelve and one, but his mother had a foreboding of something terrible tonight. When half-past one arrived, and no Sebastian, she began to cry.

"Some one ought to go up and tell your father," she said. "He may be in jail."

Jennie volunteered, but George, who was soundly sleeping, was awakened to go along with her.

"What!" said Gerhardt, astonished to see his two children.

"Bass hasn't come yet," said Jennie, and then told the story of the evening's adventure in explanation.

Gerhardt left his work at once, walking back with his two children to a point where he could turn off to go to the jail. He guessed what had happened, and his heart was troubled.

"Is that so, now!" he repeated nervously, rubbing his clumsy hands across his wet forehead.

Arrived at the station-house, the sergeant in charge told him curtly that Bass was under arrest.

"Sebastian Gerhardt?" he said, looking over his blotter; "yes, here he is. Stealing coal and resisting an officer. Is he your boy?"

"Oh, my!" said Gerhardt, "Ach Gott!" He actually wrung his hands in distress.

"Want to see him?" asked the Sergeant.

"Yes, yes," said the father.

"Take him back, Fred," said the other to the old watchman in charge, "and let him see the boy."

When Gerhardt stood in the back room, and Sebastian was brought out all marked and tousled, he broke down and began to cry. No word could cross his lips because of his emotion.

"Don't cry, pop," said Sebastian bravely. "I couldn't help it. It's all right. I'll be out in the morning."

Gerhardt only shook with his grief.

"Don't cry," continued Sebastian, doing his very best to restrain his own tears. "I'll be all right. What's the use of crying?"

"I know, I know," said the gray-headed parent brokenly, "but I can't help it. It is my fault that I should let you do that."

"No, no, it isn't," said Sebastian. "You couldn't help it. Does mother know anything about it?"

"Yes, she knows," he returned. "Jennie and George just came up where I was and told me. I didn't know anything about it until just now," and he began to cry again.

"Well, don't you feel badly," went on Bass, the finest part of his nature coming to the surface. "I'll be all right. Just you go back to work now, and don't worry. I'll be all right."

"How did you hurt your eye?" asked the father, looking at him with red eyes.
